paraphrase: All that is to be known is summed up in two: dharmas and their nature (dharmatā). Dharmas are saṃsāra, characterized by the appearance of duality and of verbal designation, arising from unreal imagination; dharmatā is nirvāṇa, characterized by suchness without the division of grasped and grasper, of object of expression and expression.
notes: From memory of the Tibetan text (no Sanskrit); ref is the opening section; to be checked against D4022.

paraphrase: Entry into non-conceptual wisdom proceeds through the non-apprehension of objects on the basis of apprehending mind-only, and the non-apprehension of mind-only on the basis of not apprehending objects; the transformation of the basis is explained under ten headings (nature, substance, persons, distinctive features, requirements, basis, attention, application, drawbacks of its absence and benefits).
notes: Section-level; the list of ten headings is recalled and must be checked against D4022/D4023.
